fields.sample_size: single municipality (Esteio, Rio Grande do Sul; 76,137 inhabitants, density 2,751 per km2); the first operating sanitation PPP in the state (contract signed in 2018 by CORSAN with the AEGEA group); documentary sources: literature review, contracts, reports, tenders, SNIS data, minutes, institutional sites and official news; no interviews reported
fields.effect_measure: qualitative exploratory case study based on document analysis, with before-and-after coverage figures from SNIS (no inferential statistics)
fields.effect_estimate: Sewage coverage in Esteio was under 10% in 2017, before the PPP contract, and exceeded 65% in 2023, an advance of more than 55 percentage points in six years (SNIS 2023); the PPP financed six new sewage pumping stations, 2.5 km of pressure lines and 19.5 km of collection networks, an investment of about R$ 18 million (AEGEA 2024). Under the contract the private partner operates and maintains sewage collection and treatment, water services and works; in December 2022 CORSAN was bought by the AEGEA consortium for R$ 4.151 billion, and the state became supervisor and regulator through its environment secretariat and state regulatory agency. The authors argue that co-creation of value and relational governance make PPPs more legitimate and innovative and support the Law 14.026/2020 goal of universalisation by 2033; the figures are the authors' compilation from institutional documents, not an evaluation.
fields.section: Full text (Portuguese, 29 pages): Introduction (methodology paragraph); theory of value co-creation; Esteio case (contract, results); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Introduction (methodology and data sources); case section on the Esteio PPP and its results (coverage 2017 vs 2023); Rev. Dir. Cid. 17(4):1-29

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative documentary case study of the Esteio (Rio Grande do Sul) sanitation public-private partnership, with SNIS before-and-after sewage coverage; read in full text 2026-10-04. No inferential statistics and no comparison municipality.
pdf_note: Revista de Direito da Cidade 17(4):1-29, Portuguese with English abstract, 29 pages read; text scanned for the case results, theoretical sections read selectively
notes: Supplies the before-and-after coverage figures (under 10% in 2017, over 65% in 2023) and the contract arrangements that the abstract-only extraction left out; the authors are advocates of the PPP model and no counterfactual is offered.
